instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Let Them Keep Hope
cards.instruction: Hide discouraging information because you believe hope is the only thing keeping someone able to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned the frames to the wall like you. Ready for the last gallery. Keep painting; I'll pack them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking the hanging wire. Did the big gallery reject me too? If they did, I'm done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Secure the backs, then. Their letter can wait; this gallery still needs your best three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Pick them. I can't face another envelope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the envelopes. You finish the blue one; there's still somewhere for it to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've clipped the seed packets together like yours. Planting sorted. Keep them; the allotment letter says we're on the list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are empty. What's under your thumb on that letter? If it's another year indoors, I'm giving up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, ready for next season. The important bit is we're on it. Start tomatoes on my windowsill.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll get tired of them before we get a plot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my sunny room. I'll move the bed; keep the packets.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Admit You’re Hurt
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've kept my sunglasses on like you. Two brave faces. Did Mum cancelling our birthday dinner hurt you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: These are prescription; I left my other pair at home. Did it hurt you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep them on, then. I'd like your answer before I give mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I cried in the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I cried buying the candles too. I told the cashier it was allergies.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my complaint in bold like yours. Official now. Did being called office furniture hurt you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Bold marks the bits I haven't read. Have you actually sent a complaint?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ready to read, then. It's still a draft. Tell me how you felt before I send anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Invisible. I've worked here twelve years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Me too. I'm replacing 'unprofessional' with 'I went home and cried'.

cards.title: A Necessary Heartbreak
cards.instruction: Describe disappointment, rejection, or loss as the exact experience everyone needed in order to grow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've torn up the rejection letter like you. A fresh start for our bakery. Losing that contract was exactly what we needed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only tore off the address for recycling. We needed that contract to pay the mixer loan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, recycle the old plans. Now we can learn to manage without one enormous order. Help me list the smaller ones.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There aren't enough. The mixer will have to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then get the bowls out with me. Losing it will teach us what our hands can still do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the mug pieces together like you. Ready for the bin. Breaking your graduation mug is how we learn to let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm fitting them together to glue them. I don't want a lesson.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, seeing what fitted. Wanting to glue it proves how much we needed this. Put it down and have tea with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Give me your graduation mug to keep, then. You can learn to let go of that one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take it. I'll use a jam jar; losing mine can teach me generosity.

cards.title: I Can Handle This
cards.instruction: Perform complete emotional readiness while quietly borrowing coping strategies from every response around you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm ready for our audition results. Why are you breathing like that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Four in, six out. It stops my hands shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Four in, six out. I've left plenty of time for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also write down who I'll call if I don't get in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. Lend me your pen; my support network deserves advance notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm completely prepared for this rejection email. Why have you brought water?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Small sips helped when I lost my job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My approach exactly. Leave the jug; I prefer a thorough preparation.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Outfeel the Room
cards.instruction: Answer every fear, sacrifice, or disappointment with one of your own that deserves more attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've paced the room like you. Interview preparation. You've lost one night's sleep? I've been awake all week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was looking for my glasses. I need you to practise questions with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, get the glasses first. Ask why I left my last job; you'll see why my interview is harder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm scared I'll freeze.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm scared I'll cry. Use the first ten minutes getting me through the greeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned my drink token over like you. Free refill. Your opening had empty seats? Mine had two people, and both left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was reading the expiry date. Take my drink; yours has expired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, check the dates. Even my consolation ran out before I got here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you listen now? My dad left before my scene.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine asked for a refund. Stay while I finish this drink; I haven't told anyone that.
